label: Actual station operation with positive-duration causal linkage
definition: StationOperationAt R h Concrete stations u c n asserts that station bearers n and n+1 are Concrete, exist and are present at the assigned c n and c(n+1) moments of one history u, that the earlier station n+1 actually causes (in the supplied Ontic.Causes sense) the later station n, and that the existing four-rule PieceAt R u c n protocol is realized. The efficient causal influence is an additional world-relative fact, not a proof that the receiver exists because of the transmitter, not a memberwise totality cause and not merely an intrinsic capability. The ontology of signal events and the cause-of-operation interpretation still require a bridge. The bearer conjuncts and PieceAt are simply conjoined: R.out and R.issues are indexed by moment, and nothing binds stations n to those registers, so the Causes edge is not modelled signal transmission.
note: Analyst stronger actual-operation semantics for #1489, distinct from Koons's CPNPP, which directly preserves powers to influence events but does not by itself establish actual influence at every link. All host, admissibility and reliable-protocol conditions are additional open application responsibilities. Formal effect (semantic challenge on PR #1854): the existence, presence, Concrete and Causes conjuncts are idle in durationDescentOfStationPrefixes and metricallyFiniteOfCountableStationRecombination; their only formal effect is to strengthen SelectedFiniteStationCompatibility (7d1b132f) and weaken CountableStationRecombination (9cb8c0ee) relative to register-only versions. The causalPivot control is a structural surrogate: it stipulates world-independent integer succession as Causes and makes every integer Concrete, so it witnesses formal satisfiability under a stipulated relation, not causal coherence of stations.
